newsitem.title: USA: Class action suit filed against Videolan.
newsitem.headline: Class action suit filed against Videolan.

text.p: Attorneys for investors who purchased Videolan Technologies Inc securities over a period of almost seven months said Tuesday that a class action lawsuit has been filed against the company.
The suit accuses the company of making false and misleading statements to investors to the effect that it had entered into an agreement with Samsung Co of South Korea.
A Videolan spokeswoman declined to comment on the suit.
The attorneys said Videolan said Samsung committed to purchase between $50 million and $70 million worth of Videolan's VL 2000 product.
The complaint alleges the defendants misrepreseted the Samsung agreement and artificially inflated the price of Videolan's securities during the period.

The attorneys said the complaint was filed on May 9 in the United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky, Louisville Division. The class action covers the period is between November 7, 1995 and May 28, 1996. The complaint is against Videolan and some former and current officers and directors.
The plaintiffs are represented by Andrew Schatz and Jeffrey Nobel, partners with the law firm of Schatz & Nobel PC, and Ron Parry, partner with the law firm of Arnzen, Parry & Wentz PSC.
